questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country, and that the nature was different than i DK, and that it was accessible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat easy, mainly because of the other danish exchange student. We helped each other out a lot

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any upon arrival, but I did get assistance a few weeks into the semester, in changing my courses, so that it fitted my academic profile more.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. We found through Airbnb - very expensive...

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You won't necessarily join any of the clubs or activities on campus. Just because the commute to uni is very long, and takes about an hour depending on traffic.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All of the courses that I had gotten pre-approved by my own uni, wasn't offered that semester. We were told that, it may occur that some of the courses wouldn't be offered, but all ten of the courses that I had approval for wasn't offered. Made it very stressfull to find four courses within the first two weeks of arrival, and also get them approved by my home uni, before the deadline in mid September

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very confusing. But as soon as spoke to a person from go global irl, he made it a lot easier for me. Just had trouble finding the office on campus... big campus

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In-person and over mail, although through mail it is always more complicated and takes a lot longer than it has to.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very. I ended up with some quite strange courses, that doesn't really fit into my profile as much as I wanted, but it was the only available ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Depending on the expectations and requirements from their home uni, I would say that the courses you are going to take on exchange, don't expect them to fit completely in with your academic profile. See the course more as extra, that may feed in to more hobby-based interest. Although you can get lucky, especially if you don't study something in humanities or arts... typical

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Tbh I am a bit disappointed in the level of the courses... Seeing as UBC is in the top 50th universities in the world, I was really disappointed in some of my courses. I didn't expect to make myself dumber for a final paper, because I wasn't allowed to be critical of a theory, but only convey the key elements of the theory. On a 400 level course!! That was surprising, and not in a good way...

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very strange actually. In KU the settings are much more informal. I call my prof. by their first names, and they see us as peers more than students, but I don't know that much, if anything about their personal lives. Whereas at UBC, the framework is very formal, in addressing the prof. by their last names, and being seen a lot more like a student rather than a peer, but I know a lot more of private information about my profs. there. Very strange and kind of difficult to navigate.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ARTH_V/VISA_V 479 001 2025W1 Performance Actions and Approaches
PHIL_V 416A A_001 2025W1 Topics in 19th-Century Philosophy
SOCI_V 414 101 2025W1 Feminist Theory
THTR_V 443A A_001 2025W1 Women in Theatre and Film

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are in to performance art, I would highly recommend Performance Actions and Approaches with prof. Camille Georgeson-Usher. It was by far my favorite courses of my exchange. In comparison to the other courses, she didn't mind us calling her Camille, and she saw us as peers more than students. And i addition, she is doing a lot of practical and curatorial work also, so you really get hands on knowledge, and it is all very up-to-date, and she is just a really good communicator

questions.answer:
Less expensive was the groceries, gas prices, uber, dining out
More expensive buying alcohol

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would have loved to join more... Joined the ski club and the outdoor club, but both clubs felt very closed to new-comers... Really enjoyed the big pool, that was free to use!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot. Some times a bit to much, so it got confusing... I think I would have participated more, if I had lived on campus...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Joining the outdoor club, cause they have rentals like tents an such. But otherwise I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Vancouver Island - Campell River was really nice! Also rent a car and drive up to Whistler and Squamish, and do some hikes and sleep in the car - just make sure it is a place that is legal! Also highly recommend taking a longer trip to Banff! We rented a camper van and drove around Banff for four days. Was magical! Do it sooner rather than later, so it dosn't get to cold to sleep in the car. 
Also really liked Seattle, but that trip kind a depends on the situation in the u.s., but really cool city - only four hours with bus from Van

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy. Like the cheap prices a Tim Hortons, and just in general the prices on service and dining out - really nice! Hard to adjust to the bars and so closing a 2 a.m., and all the locals just going home to sleep after... Even at like house parties, they close around midnight maybe if you are lucky at 1 a.m., and people just go home to sleep - disappointing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's hard. Everybody is really busy and stressed, because they take so many courses and extra points ans such. Much easier to socializing with the other exchange students. A bit sad though. Byt doing group-work with local students in class, is a way to talk with them a bit more and a little bit informal.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People going home so early. And the very big portions of groceries - very difficult to just buy like a single banana, or one coke - you have to buy the whole thing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everybody is just really kind. Even if they say that the Canadians in Vancouver is more closed off, they are much more welcoming and friendly, than any place in Europe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go enjoy the nice weather quickly! Go in weekend-trips in the beginning - do all the hikes as soon as possible! It is true, when the rain comes it doesn't stop... It rains more than DK... Also don't spend money on whale-safari! It is really expensive, and really bad for the whales! Just take the boat to Vancouver Island or Bowen Island or such

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about your grade that much. You only need 50% and that is really easy to attain.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Cliché, but I would say the people I met. I made some really good connections and friendships that I am very fond off. Also, enjoying the nature! Banff is some of the most beautiful nature I have ever seen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finances... It is very expensive going on exchange. And you are in constant limbo as to spending money on trips and such, but also needing money for practical stuff... Very difficult

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
